title: Passive vs Active: When to Use Each
grammarTitle: Passive vs Active — Choosing the Right Voice
grammarNote: Выбор между активным и страдательным залогом — это вопрос акцента. Активный залог (active voice) акцентирует исполнителя действия: "Kamila wrote the essay." Страдательный залог (passive voice) акцентирует объект и само действие: "The essay was written." Правильный выбор зависит от контекста: что важнее — КТО или ЧТО?

grammarTable.subject: Active voice
grammarTable.example: "Kamila WROTE the essay." — We focus on Kamila (the writer).

grammarTable.subject: Passive voice
grammarTable.example: "The essay WAS WRITTEN." — We focus on the essay (the result).

grammarTable.subject: Use passive when:
grammarTable.example: "The theory was first proposed in 1859." (history, not person)

grammarTable.subject: Unknown actor:
grammarTable.example: "The window was broken." (we don't know who — passive natural)

grammarTable.subject: Obvious actor:
grammarTable.example: "The president was elected." (voters = obvious; not worth stating)

grammarExtra.title: When passive is the natural choice

rows.example: "My bike was stolen last night." (we don't know who — passive is the only natural option)
"The road was repaired." (workers repaired it, but who exactly doesn't matter)
"The sample was heated to 100°C." (the scientist's identity is irrelevant)
"Three people were arrested." / "Your application has been received."
"It was found that..." / "The data was collected from three sources."

grammarExtra.title: When active is the natural choice

rows.example: "Einstein developed the theory of relativity." (Einstein = important!)
"I met her in the library." NOT "She was met by me in the library." ✗
"We need to fix this." NOT "This needs to be fixed by us." ✗
"Mistakes were made." (Who? passive hides this) → ✅ "We made mistakes."

grammarExtra.title: The "by agent" — when to include it

rows.form: Include "by" when agent is surprising / important
rows.example: "The building was designed by a 22-year-old student." (surprising — worth mentioning!)
"The president was elected." → not "...by voters" (everyone knows)
"My phone was stolen." → not "...by someone unknown." (unnecessary)
"The cotton is picked, washed, and dried." (no need to say by whom at each step)
"Zarina annotated the books." → "The books were annotated by Zarina."
"The bridge was built in 1850." → "Workers built the bridge in 1850."
"The data is collected." → "The data was collected."
"We must check this." → "This must be checked."

grammarTip:
Активный vs Страдательный — вопрос АКЦЕНТА:

✅ Активный — когда важен исполнитель:
"Darwin proposed the theory." (Дарвин = важная фигура)

✅ Страдательный — когда важен объект/результат:
"The theory was first proposed in 1859."

✅ Страдательный — когда исполнитель неизвестен:
"My laptop was stolen." (не знаем кто)

✅ Страдательный — в научном и официальном стиле:
"The experiment was conducted three times."

⚠️ Избегай страдательного без причины:
✗ "The essay was written by me." (зачем прятать себя?)
✅ "I wrote the essay." (естественнее и честнее)

exercises.instruction: Active or passive — which is more natural?
exercises.hint: Unknown agent → passive is the most natural. "My phone WAS STOLEN." ✅

opts: The theory of relativity was developed by Einstein.
Einstein developed the theory of relativity.
The theory was by Einstein developed.
exercises.hint: Both are correct! Einstein = important (active ✅). If you want to focus on the theory (not Einstein), passive ✅ too.

exercises.text: "Workers repair the road every year." → "___ every year."
opts: The road is repaired every year.
The road was repaired every year.
exercises.correct: The road is repaired every year.
exercises.hint: Present active → Present passive: "The road IS REPAIRED every year." ✅

exercises.text: "She was met by me in the library." is more natural than "I met her in the library."
exercises.hint: In personal narrative, active is more natural. "I met her in the library." ✅ is cleaner. "She was met by me" sounds unnatural.

exercises.instruction: Should you include "by workers" in this sentence?
opts: No — agent is obvious/unimportant; omit it
exercises.correct: No — agent is obvious/unimportant; omit it
exercises.hint: When the agent is obvious (of course workers fix roads!), omit "by workers". Just: "The road is repaired." ✅

exercises.text: "Someone broke my window." → Better as passive:
exercises.hint: Unknown agent → passive natural. "My window WAS BROKEN." ✅ (we don't know who)
Modal passive: "All documents MUST BE CHECKED." ✅ (must + be + past participle)

exercises.instruction: In scientific writing, which is more common?
exercises.text: "We heated the sample to 100°C." vs "The sample was heated to 100°C."
opts: "We heated" — more natural in scientific writing
"The sample was heated" — passive more common in scientific texts
exercises.correct: "The sample was heated" — passive more common in scientific texts
exercises.hint: In scientific writing, passive is standard. The scientist's identity is usually irrelevant. ✅

exercises.text: "___ by a 22-year-old student." — Should "by" be included?
opts: Yes — the agent is surprising and worth mentioning
exercises.correct: Yes — the agent is surprising and worth mentioning
exercises.hint: Include "by + agent" when it is surprising or important. "Designed BY a 22-year-old student" = surprising! ✅
"Mistakes were made" deliberately hides who made them — this is evasive use of the passive.

exercises.text: "The essay was written by Kamila." → "Kamila ___ the essay."
exercises.hint: "Kamila WROTE the essay." — active voice, past simple. ✅

exercises.instruction: For a news report, which is more natural?
exercises.text: "The journalist wrote a report." vs "A report was written by the journalist."
opts: "A report was written by the journalist." — passive is standard in news
"The journalist wrote a report." — active is more natural
exercises.correct: "The journalist wrote a report." — active is more natural
exercises.hint: In news, active is more engaging: "The journalist WROTE a report." ✅. Passive "A report was written by the journalist" sounds awkward and overly formal.

questions.text: When is passive voice most appropriate?
opts: When you want to hide the action
When the result/action matters more than who did it
questions.correct: When the result/action matters more than who did it
questions.hint: Passive emphasises the action/result over the actor.

questions.text: "Darwin proposed the theory." — Why active here?
opts: Past tense only works with active
Darwin is important — active highlights him
The sentence is too short for passive
questions.correct: Darwin is important — active highlights him
questions.hint: When the agent is important and interesting, active voice highlights them better.

opts: We don't know who stole it — passive is natural
Active: "Someone stole my car" sounds wrong
questions.correct: We don't know who stole it — passive is natural
questions.hint: Unknown agent → passive is the natural choice. "My car WAS STOLEN." ✅

questions.text: Convert to passive: "Workers repaired the road."
questions.hint: "Workers repaired (past active)" → "The road WAS REPAIRED." (past passive)

questions.text: "The president was elected." — Why is "by voters" omitted?
opts: Voters are obvious — everyone knows who elects presidents
questions.correct: Voters are obvious — everyone knows who elects presidents
questions.hint: When the agent is obvious, omit "by + agent". No need to state the obvious. ✅

questions.text: "I wrote the essay." — Is "The essay was written by me" better?
opts: Yes — passive is always more formal
No — in personal writing, active is more natural
They are identical in meaning and style
questions.correct: No — in personal writing, active is more natural
questions.hint: In personal writing and narrative, active voice is cleaner. "I wrote the essay." ✅

questions.text: "The sample was heated to 100°C." — Why passive in a science report?
opts: The scientist's name is always irrelevant
Scientific writing focuses on the process, not the person
questions.correct: Scientific writing focuses on the process, not the person
questions.hint: Science writing uses passive because the method/result matters more than who specifically did it.

questions.text: "Mistakes were made." is an example of clear, precise passive writing.
questions.hint: "Mistakes were made" is EVASIVE passive — it deliberately hides who made them.
Modal passive: modal + BE + past participle. "This MUST BE CHECKED." ✅

opts: When the agent is surprising, interesting, or important
questions.correct: When the agent is surprising, interesting, or important
questions.hint: Include "by + agent" when it adds value. Omit it when obvious or unknown.

questions.text: "The theory was proposed by Darwin." → Active:
questions.hint: Active: "Darwin PROPOSED the theory." — the passive subject (the theory) becomes the object. ✅

questions.text: "Three people were arrested." — This is used in:
questions.hint: News uses passive to focus on the event and victim/subject: "Three people were arrested." ✅
Present passive: "The road IS REPAIRED every autumn." ✅

questions.text: In a process description of how bread is made, which is more natural?
opts: Bakers mix the dough. Bakers put it in the oven...
The dough is mixed. It is put in the oven...
questions.correct: The dough is mixed. It is put in the oven...
questions.hint: Process descriptions use passive — the baker's identity doesn't change with each step. Passive reads more naturally. ✅

questions.text: "The building was designed by a 22-year-old." — Why include "by a 22-year-old"?
opts: Because you must always include the agent
The young age is surprising — worth mentioning
questions.correct: The young age is surprising — worth mentioning
questions.hint: "By a 22-year-old" is surprising! Including the agent here adds interesting information. ✅

questions.text: Which sentence is in active voice and most natural for personal narrative?
questions.hint: "I visited the library." ✅ — active voice is most natural for personal narrative. "A library was visited by me" is awkward.
